2609.11391.title: Buyer Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Environmental Governance and Supplier Environmental Controversies: An Organizational Information Processing and Signaling
2609.11391.paper_summary: Environmental controversies in global supply chains pose significant risks for global buyers. This study examines whether overseas suppliers' exposure to buyers' artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled environmental governance reduces supplier environmental controversies. Drawing on organizational information processing theory and signaling theory, we investigate how suppliers' exposure to AI-enabled governance influences their environmental controversies and the institutional contingencies under which this effect varies. Using text analysis to measure buyer AI-enabled environmental governance, we analyze panel data on 2,505 suppliers of U.S.-listed firms across 41 countries from 2020 to 2024 with multidimensional fixed-effects models. We find that suppliers' exposure to buyer AI-enabled environmental governance is negatively associated with supplier environmental controversies in the following year. This negative relationship is stronger in supplier countries with higher AI readiness and regulatory quality. The study contributes to research on AI-enabled sustainability governance and sustainable supply chain risk management.
2609.11391.paper_summary_zh: 環境爭議在全球供應鏈中對全球買家構成重大風險。這項研究探討海外供應商面對買家的人工智慧（AI）驅動的環境治理是否會減少供應商的環境爭議。基於組織資訊處理理論和信號理論，我們研究供應商面對AI驅動治理如何影響他們的環境爭議，以及這一影響在何種制度情境下會有所變化。使用文本分析來衡量買家的AI驅動環境治理，我們分析了2020年至2024年間來自41個國家的2,505家美國上市公司的供應商的面板數據，並使用多維固定效應模型。我們發現，供應商面對買家的AI驅動環境治理與供應商在接下來一年內的環境爭議呈負相關。這種負相關在AI準備度和監管質量較高的供應商國家中更為明顯。這項研究對於AI驅動的可持續治理和可持續供應鏈風險管理的研究作出了貢獻。
2609.11391.author: Yongchao Martin Ma et.al.
